paragraphs.title: The Mission of Consolation and Redemption

easy.explanation: The messenger was sent to preach good tidings unto the meek.
easy.q: To whom was the messenger sent to preach good tidings?

easy.explanation: The passage says he was sent to bind up the brokenhearted.
easy.q: What would the messenger do for the brokenhearted?

easy.explanation: The Lord would give them beauty for ashes.
easy.q: What would be given to those who mourned in Zion instead of ashes?

medium.explanation: Liberty means freedom, especially for those held captive.
medium.q: What does “liberty” mean in the phrase “to proclaim liberty to the captives”?

answers: Mourning is replaced with joy and praise
medium.explanation: The passage speaks of the oil of joy, the garment of praise, and comfort for those who mourn.
medium.q: What change is described for those who mourn?

answers: Because they are strong in battle
Because they are the Lord’s planting for his glory
medium.explanation: They are called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that he might be glorified.
medium.q: Why are the people called “trees of righteousness”?

answers: Good news, healing, liberty, and comfort
challenge.explanation: The mission includes preaching good tidings, binding up the brokenhearted, proclaiming liberty, and comforting mourners.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the messenger’s mission?

answers: Both describe a time of favor and consolation
Both describe the building of cities
challenge.explanation: The acceptable year introduces the message of the Lord’s favor and comfort.
challenge.q: How is the acceptable year of the Lord connected with comforting mourners?

answers: A change from mourning to honor, joy, and praise
challenge.explanation: These images describe the transformation of the mourners’ condition.
challenge.q: What do beauty, the oil of joy, and the garment of praise represent?

paragraphs.title: Restoration of the Land and Israel’s Status

answers: The old wastes and desolate cities
easy.explanation: The people would build the old wastes, raise up former desolations, and repair the waste cities.
easy.q: What would be rebuilt in the days of restoration?

easy.explanation: The passage says that strangers would stand and feed their flocks.

answers: The Priests of the Lord and Ministers of God
easy.explanation: The people would be named the Priests of the Lord and the Ministers of our God.

medium.explanation: Here, wastes are ruined or deserted places that will be rebuilt.
medium.q: What does “wastes” mean in “they shall build the old wastes”?

answers: Tend flocks and work in farming
medium.explanation: They would be plowmen and vinedressers and would help care for the flocks.
medium.q: What work would the sons of the alien do for Israel?

medium.explanation: The passage promises a double portion and everlasting joy instead of shame and confusion.
medium.q: What would replace shame and confusion?

answers: The land is rebuilt, and the people receive the status of the Lord’s priests
The cities are destroyed, and the people go into exile
Foreigners become the rulers of Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage describes both the restoration of the land and the elevation of Israel’s status.
challenge.q: How are the restoration of the cities and Israel’s changed status connected?

answers: It shows that restoration is connected with justice rather than oppression
It describes only the priests’ duties
It explains how vineyards are cultivated
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises to direct their work in truth and make an everlasting covenant with them.
challenge.q: Why does the Lord’s love of judgment and hatred of robbery matter in this passage?

answers: They will acknowledge them as the seed blessed by the Lord
They will drive Israel from the land
They will stop working the land
challenge.explanation: All who see them will acknowledge that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.
challenge.q: What will happen when the nations recognize Israel’s descendants?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Joy and the Praise of Redemption

easy.explanation: The speaker says, “I will greatly rejoice in the Lord.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker greatly rejoice?

answers: Garments of salvation and a robe of righteousness
easy.explanation: God clothed the speaker with the garments of salvation and covered him with the robe of righteousness.
easy.q: What garments did God give the speaker?

easy.explanation: The passage compares the adornment to a bridegroom and a bride.
easy.q: What comparison is used for the speaker’s joyful adornment?

medium.explanation: The garments symbolize the salvation and righteousness provided by God.
medium.q: What do “garments of salvation” and “the robe of righteousness” express?

answers: Like plants growing from the earth and a garden
medium.explanation: The passage compares God’s work to the earth and garden bringing forth plants.
medium.q: How is the growth of redemption described?

medium.explanation: The passage says righteousness and praise will spring forth before all the nations.
medium.q: Before whom will the Lord cause righteousness and praise to spring forth?

answers: Both express honor, joy, and renewal
challenge.explanation: The joyful adornment emphasizes the honor and renewal brought by salvation.
challenge.q: How does the image of the bridegroom and bride relate to redemption?

answers: Redemption develops and becomes visible like natural growth
Redemption remains hidden from the nations
challenge.explanation: As the earth and garden bring forth plants, God causes righteousness and praise to appear.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the comparison between a garden and God’s work?

answers: With joy and rejoicing in God
challenge.explanation: The speaker rejoices greatly in the Lord and says that his soul is joyful in God.
challenge.q: How do God’s people respond to the message of salvation?
